notes.title: Development : Ballistic Missile Submarine
notes.content:
Knights with swords galloping across the plains, engaging in fierce battles...

long ago, that's what war looked like. Then, the miracles of industrialization by modern civilization changed everything. Weapons became more powerful and complex. Making tanks and fighter jets required loads of factories. So, wars began to be fought in factories. The path to victory was outproducing the enemy in weaponry. 

But this was a tough task. Then the generals had a brilliant idea: destroy the enemy's factories.  A new era of warfare had begun. 

Around the same time, scientists were working on a new bomb that could obliterate entire factories and cities. It was perfect for this new age of war. Everything was there at the right time. To quote Victor Hugo: [i]"Nothing is more powerful than an idea whose time has come."[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/d3b5e20ae20d57ad5967937b0fa86a3e8f1b9303.jpg[/img]



[b]Submarines and Nuclear Weapons[/b]
We often think of submarines as smart hunters, but that’s only half the story. The other half is way more audacious. They're the most powerful fleet in human history, trusted with the ability to launch hundreds of nuclear warheads and wipe out entire continents in an instant. 

Of course, this system is always controversial and comes with many paradoxes. I want to focus on these themes in the game's story mode, but for now, let's talk about more practical issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/91ad7e4d600ca985bce843209df0034900dc7dc1.jpg[/img]



[b]The Problem of Reality and Boredom[/b]
Playing simulation games often reveals a harsh truth: real life can be pretty dull. I once flew a Boeing 787 from London to New York in Microsoft Flight Simulator, sitting for seven hours monitoring the autopilot. While I love airplanes, I would prefer a more meaningful holiday. 

By analogy, missions for strategic missile submarines (SSBNs) would be incredibly boring. Their main duty is to remain undetected—no flashy battles, no tense chases—just waiting in a safe zone for orders. 

This fundamental dullness of reality poses a major challenge for games and movies. Everyone wants to play iconic submarines like Project 941, but without some drama, the fun is limited.



[b]The Issue of Game World Size[/b]
Even if we come up with an enjoyable SSBN mission, another problem arises. Our game world is 100km by 100km, so when ballistic missiles are launched, they fly out of view. We can't even see our targets. 

This is a common issue in all 3D games. As weapon ranges increase, the game world expands, leading to long travel times and barely visible targets—just icons on the screen. Map-based games like Hearts of Iron excel in this, offering the best way to enjoy strikes across the globe, but what we're creating is different. 

Hence, we even question whether players should be able to select strategic missile submarines in the first place. We have already completed several 3D models. However, as previously mentioned, it's worth rethinking how to incorporate these weapons into the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/b8263576b77ea2b53b87c61009fceed753118e50.jpg[/img]



[b]Simple Proposals[/b]
For example, how about making SSBNs and nuclear weapons available as special items once the game is completed? They wouldn't appear in main missions but could provide fun for SSBN enthusiasts. Alternatively, allowing their use in specific story missions could be more realistic, considering military command structures. But there will still be players who want to use nuclear missiles more freely. If you have any interesting suggestions, please leave a comment!



[b]Project Progress[/b]
Development of nuclear weapons in the game is going well. I researched YouTube footage of nuclear tests and created the following sequence.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/e79f2d72a745cc5afcc6050c31ff21352074c254.jpg[/img]
 Unlike dry deserts, condensation rings appear at Pacific testing sites. We've conducted multiple tests to replicate these in the game engine. It's not perfect yet, but it looks good as a prototype. 

[previewyoutube=VmD6jbSOIXU;full]https://youtu.be/VmD6jbSOIXU[/previewyoutube]

Nuclear weapons will be a recurring theme throughout the game. There's much more to delve into, but it's too lengthy to cover here, so I'll save it for another time. 

Our recent focus has also been on game design. Technically, the game is almost complete, but as a play experience, it still needs work. I want the game to be intuitive for players who are new to submarines, which requires additional research. As always, I'm open to ideas!

notes.title: Development : Explosion Artist
notes.content:
I remember playing GTA5 back in 2013 and being absolutely thrilled by the thick, immersive explosion effects. I would steal a tank from the military base and go on a rampage, destroying every vehicle in sight. Those explosions were addictive!

Now, I’ve finally transitioned to being the one creating explosions (safely, of course). A famous Japanese sculptor once said, “Art is explosion.” He meant it metaphorically, as a way to express emotions. But I believe "explosions are art". This isn’t a metaphor; creating beautiful explosions requires an artistic touch. Nowadays, these experts are known as VFX artists.

The only problem was, I had no experience or knowledge as a VFX artist. But then again, most developers are not great at predicting future problems, which is why game release dates get delayed so often.

Feeling lost, I browsed the Unity Asset Store and found some amazing products. The catch? They were designed for medieval siege engines in fantasy games or Molotov cocktails for zombie apocalypses. Modern warfare weapons don’t explode like that.

However, they were generous enough to let me break down and customize their products. So, I learned how to use VFX Graph (Unity’s GPU-based effects engine) and, with a lot of tweaking and custom coding, created the effects I needed. Here’s what I’ve achieved in the past week:

Underwater Explosion
Expands in a circular pattern, then contracts, leaving bubbles behind.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/2f159f9098eb261a8d7867bd5930a5f8bdd19b3b.jpg[/img]


Shallow Explosion
When trapped energy reaches the water surface, it releases suddenly, sending water high into the air.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/0d91cf5b7aaba2a7166255f006e0dc366c4b39eb.jpg[/img]


Anti-Ship Missile Explosion
When it hits a thin target, small fragments penetrate and scatter to the other side.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/9dd2aac3978df547e6f2f0decf9eab142cceec03.jpg[/img]


You can watch the explosion videos on YouTube. These are still in development, so they don’t represent the final quality.
[previewyoutube=BOIdNaHbB5I;full][/previewyoutube]


What I’ve shown today is just a small part of the current tasks. There’s still a massive amount of work to be done, and honestly, I sigh every time I look at the roadmap. The team is working on coding the underwater missile launch system, creating trailer footage, and 3D modeling various objects. Please bear with us until the game is playable!

notes.title: Development : Behind the Nuclear Power
notes.content:
When I was in elementary school, I couldn’t trust the ground beneath my feet. I feared it might one day sink into a sea of magma. Fortunately, that was a misunderstanding on my part. When you look at a cross-section of the Earth, it seems like there’s a vast amount of molten rock beneath the crust we live on. But in reality, it’s not liquid. Due to the high pressure underground, it remains solid even at high temperatures.

This phenomenon was discovered hundreds of years ago, back when science was still called alchemy. By applying high pressure to a substance, you can prevent it from melting or boiling. This discovery revolutionized navies centuries later.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/f8c5cfd2177abf82d188605c4ca28dfab16e7dff.png[/img]


[b]Pressurized Water Reactor[/b]
One of the critical issues in reactor development was finding a way to isolate water contaminated with radioactive materials. As water passes through the reactor core, a nuclear reaction called the (n-p) reaction is triggered by the fast-moving neutrons. This reaction transforms the oxygen atoms in the water into radioactive isotopes of nitrogen. Although these isotopes have a short lifespan and decay back into oxygen within seconds, they emit powerful gamma rays in the process. 

When contaminated steam is sent to the turbines, it generates strong radiation around them. This means that no one can approach the turbine area for some time after operation. Additionally, extra shielding is required in the turbine room, which adds weight and takes up space—something undesirable in a cramped submarine. Moreover, in emergencies, immediate repairs to water leaks are necessary. Having inaccessible areas in such situations is terrifying.

To address this, reactors with two separate water circulation systems, known as the primary and secondary loops, were devised. Contaminants circulate only within the primary loop. The secondary loop is completely isolated, ensuring that the turbines and other systems are not exposed to radiation.

However, this method has its drawbacks. The thermal conversion efficiency is poor. When transferring heat from the primary loop to the secondary loop through thin alloy pipes, some energy is lost. This means that the primary loop needs to be at a higher temperature to convert the water in the secondary loop into steam. So, let’s apply pressure to the water.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/87704cbe540fa14dbe7800c2e2cc984d56cf64e9.png[/img]


A typical submarine reactor is called a Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR). Pressurized water means exactly that—water kept under pressure so it can remain in liquid form at high temperatures. Pressurized water doesn’t boil at 100°C; it can reach much higher temperatures. This ability to heat water to extraordinary temperatures led to the creation of nuclear-powered submarines.


[b]A True Nuclear Submarine[/b]
Despite the iconic term “nuclear submarine,” traditional games have rarely emphasized the differences. Simply changing the 3D model of the hull isn’t enough. I wanted to make the differences in power plants more distinct. Nuclear submarines are powerful but complex, while diesel submarines are simple and easy, though they require battery charging. Therefore, it was necessary to create an operable reactor system.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/9c3e6d0005fdceb406108f1e09074c38451c1c1d.png[/img]


In this game, you can operate a Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR). However, since I couldn’t find blueprints for submarine reactors, I based the design on standard commercial power plants. Instead of actual reactor physics, a simplified thermal equilibrium model is used. The turbine output is a function of the secondary loop pressure. Since pressure is a function of temperature and volume, you can ultimately control the parameters with control rods and valves. The temperature difference between loops is calculated as a thermal equilibrium model, which includes additional pumps to circulate the fluid at sufficient speed.

A well-designed reactor system has stability. Theoretically, when the throttle is opened, the temperature drops, and the water density slightly increases. This makes it easier for neutrons to slow down, increasing the nuclear reaction and returning to the original temperature. Submarine reactors, which need to change output frequently, are likely designed this way. However, since I couldn’t obtain definitive information, it hasn’t been replicated yet. Nevertheless, I find this more enjoyable as a game. A bit of busyness adds to the fun.

Players will operate the reactor control rods, cooling system, turbines, and valves. These systems are unique and may be a bit confusing at first. However, as you get better, you’ll be able to control the output with minimal operations.


The next video shows the reactor control panel currently under development. This video has been accelerated 12x.
[previewyoutube=QMTtphE1uYg;full][/previewyoutube]


I am aware of submarines equipped with other types of powertrains. France is one example. Additionally, traditional diesel-electric submarines are popular worldwide. Therefore, I plan to implement three types of designs:


[list]
[*]PWR
[*]PWR + electric motor
[*]Diesel-electric + AIP
[/list]

Of course, there are submarines that don’t fit into these categories, but for now, they will be substituted with the closest match. However, I might do additional programming for legendary boats like Project 705. I love that boat.


Some submarines from the Soviet Union and the United States were equipped with more advanced liquid metal cooled reactors, which use liquid metal instead of water. These submarines were a significant technical success. However, considering the need to maintain a fleet at low cost, they were clearly an excessive investment. It was just as important to avoid bankrupting the country as it was to deter war.


Finally, I’m not an expert in reactor engineering, so I don’t fully understand the actual mechanisms. If you find any missing parts, please let me know in the comments! Community collaboration will make the game better!

notes.title: Development : Torpedo in the water
notes.content:
Stealth is not the only reason submarines are said to be the most powerful. Modern torpedoes have unparalleled power on the battlefield. 

Since the advent of the self-guided torpedo, all kinds of decoys have been developed to fool it. However, it is now known that many of them do not work well enough. The torpedo's search algorithm is designed to either ignore the decoy or return and attack again even if it misses the enemy. In other words, it is very advantageous to the attacker.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/57b4893d490620d1b24818c4fc48c8b104c619cc.jpg[/img]

Asymmetries like this are also a bit tricky to create games. Looking back at other games, it is clear that unbalanced weapons ruin the battlefield.


Therefore, I have established these policies.

[b]- Avoid making the torpedo’s search algorithm more advanced.[/b]
Simplifying maneuver patterns during re-attacks allows defenders to avoid them. It also does not have advanced target identification capabilities such as image recognition. However, it can be guided manually as long as the wire is connected. This means that torpedo guidance performance is dependent on player skill.

[b]- Adjust torpedo’s range, speed and turning performance in moderation.[/b]
The range of some torpedoes can reach 50 km. On the other hand, a typical game map is 100 km square, so if a battle occurs in the center of the map, the torpedoes will chase you even if you escape to the limits of the play area. It may seem a little too strong. Therefore, the torpedo's key performance parameters will be adjusted through test play to achieve the right balance.


This is a typical search pattern of the torpedo.
[olist]
[*]A wire is connected to the torpedo that has just been fired and the manual control mode is enabled.
[*]When the torpedo reaches the wire length limit, it switches to the self-search mode. In this mode, it searches for targets in a straight line, S-shape, or circular pattern.
[*]When the torpedo finds the target, it switches to tracking mode and begins its approach to the target.
[*]If the torpedo loses the contact, it will again enter search mode, but this time it will execute a circle search pattern in the direction in which it had detected the signal just before missed the target. If the torpedo finds the target while searching in a circle, it will attempt to approach again.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/89a2ac16d8ea5d5c2f0f6bb09b52d18015f6fa5f.jpg[/img]

This is a simplified figure for illustrative purposes; the actual developed version is a bit more complex. In addition, torpedoes have passive and active sensors, each of which has different search capabilities. They also move a little differently in tracking mode and hit different positions of the ship.


We wanna implement various other types of torpedoes. For example, a rocket torpedo that uses supercavitation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033547/f8b304965a762619e7cbd49577dc57682217c079.jpg[/img]

However, first I have to make a 3D model. Since I am coding and modeling all by myself at the same time (and going to university during the day), the process takes a bit more time. So I ask my friends to help me with modeling and coding. Please be looking forward to updating while watching pigeons in the park or solving the P≠NP forecast!
